llm.summary: This writing skill is not clearly malicious, but it asks for broad command, file, API, and credential capabilities that are not well scoped for article drafting.

dimensions.detail: Research and local output files are proportionate to the purpose, but general exec authority and unspecified API credential usage are overbroad for a writing assistant without concrete scoping or containment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains only a Markdown skill file and no executable install scripts or bundled code. The frontmatter tool declaration is the main authority request.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main article workflow is reasonably described, but later quick-start and troubleshooting sections introduce API keys, external connections, command execution, and file processing without naming providers, allowed commands, data sent, or required user confirmations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact describes writing article outputs under output/{slug}/article.md and includes an optional callback_url, but does not show background persistence, startup hooks, destructive actions, or credential storage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is long-form research article drafting, source organization, outlining, editing, and writing, but the artifact also declares exec/read/glob/grep tools and later describes generic file processing, API integration, command execution, and bulk processing beyond the writing workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It may be useful for drafting research articles, but only enable it in an environment where broad file reads, command execution, and unspecified API credentials are acceptable. Avoid giving it sensitive directories, secrets, or production credentials unless the publisher narrows the allowed commands and names the external services used.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The concern about scope expansion is supported: lines describing generic file handling, command execution, and information retrieval go beyond the article-crafting purpose.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The concern about API keys and external API use is supported because the artifact asks for API keys and credentials but does not identify providers or data boundaries.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The quick-start concern is supported because it shifts into configuring API keys, initializing connections, processing files, and executing commands rather than only research and drafting.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The exec concern is supported by the declared exec tool and command-execution instructions; the artifact mentions whitelisting but provides no actual allowlist or narrow use case.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The disclosure concern is supported: file outputs are disclosed early, but command execution, API credentials, and broader side effects are introduced later and remain under-specified.
